title: Can You Really Change Your Face Shape?

scenes.narration: The internet says you can reshape your jawline. Your skeleton has other ideas.
scenes.art: a young adult looking in a mirror at their jawline, their reflection shown as a friendly cartoon skull x-ray with a skeptical raised eyebrow

scenes.narration: Your face is built in layers. Bone at the bottom, then muscle, fat and fluid on top.
scenes.art: a clean cartoon cross-section diagram of a human face showing layers: bone, red muscle, yellow fat, and a light blue fluid layer, educational infographic

scenes.narration: Bone first. Mewing, pressing your tongue to the roof of your mouth, has no controlled studies showing it reshapes an adult jaw.
scenes.art: a cartoon side profile of a young adult pressing their tongue to the roof of the mouth, a big question mark floating next to their jaw

scenes.narration: And bone smashing? Surgeons warn it can cause fractures, nerve damage and a crooked face. Please don't.
scenes.art: a stern friendly cartoon surgeon in scrubs holding up a hand in a stop gesture, a big red warning sign beside them

scenes.narration: Muscle can change a little. In one small study, twenty weeks of facial exercises made cheeks look fuller.
scenes.art: a middle-aged woman doing a facial exercise with puffed cheeks, a calendar with many checked days behind her

scenes.narration: But it was only sixteen people, with no control group. Promising, not proven.
scenes.art: a small group of sixteen simple cartoon people standing in a row next to an empty dashed outline where a control group should be

scenes.narration: Fat is the big one. Facial fat tracks body weight so closely that people can estimate weight from a face alone.
scenes.art: an observer studying a portrait gallery of different faces, a glowing scale icon floating above the frames
scenes.cite: de Jager et al., Frontiers in Psychology 2018

scenes.narration: And faces are sensitive. In one study, people noticed a change of under two BMI points just from someone's face.
scenes.art: two nearly identical cartoon portraits side by side with a tiny difference in cheek fullness, a magnifying glass hovering between them
scenes.cite: Re & Rule, Soc Psychol Personal Sci 2016

scenes.narration: And fluid changes day to day. Salt, alcohol and short sleep can all make your face look puffier.
scenes.art: a sleepy young adult in the morning with a slightly puffy face, a salty snack bag and an empty glass on the nightstand

scenes.narration: So you can't hack your skeleton. But the layers on top are where real change happens.
scenes.art: a confident young adult silhouette with a calm glowing outline, layers of soft light peeling around the face like a reveal, hopeful sunrise colors

scenes.narration: Have you ever tried mewing? Be honest.

post.title: Can you really change your face shape? (mewing, bone smashing, face yoga) 🦴
post.description:
Your face is built in layers: bone, muscle, fat and fluid. Here's what the evidence says each one can and can't do. Bone smashing is dangerous: don't try it.

Sources:
Alam et al. (2018) JAMA Dermatology
de Jager, Coetzee & Coetzee (2018) Frontiers in Psychology
Re & Rule (2016) Social Psychological and Personality Science
Mater Health (2026) surgeons' warning on bone smashing
